reason: The cited lines show the tool gathering and returning local/host information: available server entries including pid and command, localhost URLs/ports, and tool metadata obtained from local Next.js MCP servers. That supports SECRET because non-public local host/localhost-derived data is returned into context. The returned tool name/description/inputSchema and server command values come from local servers/processes and can be controlled by the application/server being inspected, so UNTRUSTED is supported. The lines do not show arbitrary host code execution, nor do they show agent-supplied data being sent to an attacker-readable destination; they only list/probe local servers and return metadata.
